top.title: Nasarawa pensioners begin enforcement of ₦4bn court order
top.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia A group of 601 retired civil servants in Nasarawa State has commenced enforcement of a court order directing the recovery of over ₦4 billion in outstanding gratuities and other entitlements owed them by the state government. The pensioners, under the aegis of the Concerned Group of Nasarawa State Pensioners, secured a consent judgment against the state government in 2020 over the alleged non-payment of their retirement benefits. Their spokespersons, Mr Simon Auna and Mallam Usman Adamu, disclosed the development while speaking with journalists in Lafia on Friday. The group said it subsequently obtained an order from the National Industrial Court, Makurdi, awarding 25 per cent post-judgment interest on the judgment sum, bringing the total amount being sought to over ₦4 billion. According to the pensioners, following the alleged failure of the state government to comply with the judgment, their lawyers approached the Senior District Court in Makurdi, presided over by Justice Ada Jack. The court subsequently directed six commercial banks to release funds belonging to the Nasarawa State Government, amounting to over ₦4 billion, for payment to the affected retirees. In a move to enforce the order, the pensioners’ legal team, accompanied by court bailiffs, visited some branches of one of the commercial banks in Makurdi, Benue State, where they removed some movable properties. Speaking on the development, counsel to the pensioners, Mrs Doofan Sefa-Aii, said the legal team would continue to operate within the law to ensure full recovery of the funds owed the retirees. Another counsel, Mr Awo Matthew, appealed to the Nasarawa State Government and the banks involved to allow the legal process to take its course, considering the hardship the pensioners had endured while pursuing payment of their entitlements. However, the Director of Corporate Services and Arbitration at the Nasarawa State Ministry of Justice, Mr Usman Aliyu, said the state government had taken all necessary legal steps, including filing a motion for a stay of execution of the court order. Meanwhile, Adamu, who is the group’s Lafia Local Government Chairman, and Auna, its Legal Adviser, described the court order as a significant breakthrough after years of seeking payment of their entitlements. They said the development had renewed their hope of recovering the outstanding benefits. The pensioners reaffirmed their determination to pursue their entitlements through lawful means until the matter was resolved. top.title: Zulum offers soldiers N50,000 each, logistics for Borno deployment
top.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced a ₦50,000 welfare support for each soldier preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe communities in the state, alongside a pledge to provide operational logistics to strengthen security. Zulum gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area, where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. The governor said the visit was aimed at exploring measures to improve security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, a strategic economic corridor linking several communities in eastern Borno State. He noted that the highway was vital to trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities, stressing that improved security would enable residents to travel safely, move agricultural produce and rebuild their livelihoods. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe, the governor pledged to provide operational logistics and sustained welfare support. He also announced a payment of ₦50,000 to each soldier preparing for the deployment to the two communities. Koshebe has previously suffered deadly attacks by suspected Boko Haram insurgents. On November 28, 2020, insurgents attacked rice farmers working in fields around the community, killing more than 100 people, many of whom were seasonal farm labourers from Sokoto State. Similarly, in November 2023, suspected insurgents attacked farmers harvesting rice in the Karkut and Koshebe areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 people, while others were reported missing. Zulum’s administration has continued to provide logistics and welfare assistance to security agencies as part of efforts to support military operations, improve security and facilitate the return of displaced residents to their communities. The governor was accompanied on the visit by the member representing Monguno/Nganzai/Marte Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Engr. Bukar Talba; member representing Dikwa Constituency in the Borno State House of Assembly, Mohammed Zakariya; Commissioner for Information and Internal Security, Professor Usman Tar; Commissioner for Local Government and Emirate Affairs, Sugun Mai Mele; and other senior government officials. top.title: COVID-19 loans must be repaid, NIRSAL MFB insists
top.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief NIRSAL Microfinance Bank (NMFB) has clarified that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility (TCF) was an intervention loan, not a grant, stressing that beneficiaries are obligated to repay the funds. The bank said deductions from the accounts of beneficiaries who accessed the facility would continue until their outstanding loans were fully liquidated, in line with the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism. In a statement issued in Abuja at the weekend, the bank explained that the GSI framework allows financial institutions to recover outstanding loan obligations from eligible accounts linked to borrowers’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs), subject to applicable regulatory guidelines. The bank said the clarification became necessary to address concerns surrounding loan recoveries and reassure customers and members of the public of its commitment to transparency, accountability and responsible banking practices. It explained that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility was introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to support households and businesses affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the bank, all beneficiaries were required to accept electronic offer letters before disbursement, with the documents clearly outlining the terms and conditions of the facility, including repayment obligations and recovery mechanisms in cases of default. “Regarding the recovery process, the Bank operates within the applicable regulatory framework, including the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism approved by the Central Bank of Nigeria,” it stated. NIRSAL MFB, however, acknowledged concerns raised by some beneficiaries over the timing and amounts of deductions, outstanding loan balances and access to repayment information. The bank said it took the complaints seriously, noting that customers must have access to accurate information about their loan accounts. It stressed that the deductions were intended to settle outstanding contractual obligations, adding that beneficiaries who disputed deductions or identified discrepancies in their repayment records should contact the bank for individual account reconciliation. “Where any beneficiary has concerns about deductions made, discrepancies in repayment records or the status of an outstanding balance, such cases should be brought to the bank’s attention for individual account reconciliation and appropriate resolution,” it said. The bank assured that legitimate complaints would be investigated and that any discrepancies established during the reconciliation process would receive the necessary attention. It urged beneficiaries seeking clarification on their loan status, repayment history or outstanding obligations to contact the bank through its officially designated customer service channels. top.title: Customs intercepts live sea turtle at Nigeria-Benin border
top.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Seme Area Command, has intercepted a live endangered sea turtle allegedly being smuggled through a footpath linking Nigeria and the Republic of Benin. The Olive Ridley Sea Turtle, scientifically known as Lepidochelys olivacea, was intercepted during a routine patrol by Customs officers at about 10.30pm on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The command said the officers sighted a suspicious individual carrying a sack along the border route, but the suspect abandoned the bag and fled into a nearby bush upon noticing the patrol team. According to a statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Customs, John Tunde Ayagbalo, examination of the abandoned sack revealed the live sea turtle concealed inside. He said the animal was immediately secured and kept in safe custody before being handed over to relevant wildlife authorities for proper care, rehabilitation and eventual release into its natural habitat. The Acting Customs Area Controller, Seme Area Command, Deputy Comptroller Norman Olisah Alumanah, described the interception as a demonstration of the vigilance and professionalism of officers in tackling wildlife trafficking. Alumanah warned smugglers, poachers and their collaborators against using the nation’s borders as corridors for illegal wildlife trade, adding that the command had intensified patrols, surveillance and intelligence gathering across its area of responsibility. He also called on residents of border communities to provide credible intelligence to support the fight against wildlife trafficking. The Customs boss said the command would complement enforcement operations with stakeholder education and sensitisation on endangered species, their ecological importance and the legal implications of their unauthorised trade. Wildlife trafficking remains a major environmental crime, threatening biodiversity and the survival of endangered species through illegal exploitation for meat, eggs, shells, traditional medicine and the exotic pet trade. Nigeria is a signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which regulates international trade in endangered wildlife and plant species. The convention is domesticated in Nigeria through the Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act, Cap E9, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. top.description: By Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has completed the 21-day monitoring of all 62 contacts linked to the imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease (BVD), a form of Ebola disease, confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026, with no secondary infections recorded. The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Friday during a media briefing in Abuja, saying the last contact had been discharged from monitoring after testing negative for the virus. Idris said 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period, but laboratory tests confirmed that none had contracted the disease. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case. “A total of 62 contacts were identified, placed in quarantine and followed up by our public health teams. During the monitoring period, 13 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease, and all tested negative,” he said. The index case was a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman, who tested positive for the virus in Abuja on October 20. She was subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26. Providing an update on her condition, Idris said the woman had recovered and been discharged from a hospital in Geneva. He also disclosed that seven additional suspected cases were reported and investigated in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the past three weeks. All seven cases tested negative for the virus. However, the NCDC chief cautioned against interpreting the completion of contact monitoring as a formal declaration that the outbreak was over. He explained that such a declaration would depend on established public health criteria and findings from continued surveillance. “It is important to note that the completion of contact monitoring does not, by itself, constitute a formal declaration that an outbreak is over. Such a determination must be based on the applicable public health criteria and the findings of ongoing surveillance. “Nigeria therefore remains vigilant, particularly given the continued occurrence of Ebola virus disease in the DRC,” he said. top.title: 2027: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi not there for Nigeria — Sule Lamido
top.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Jigawa State Governor and PDP chieftain, Sule Lamido, has dismissed President Bola Tinubu, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, as unsuitable options for Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general election. Lamido stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, where he was asked which of the three political figures could attract the Northern vote in the forthcoming presidential election. Giving his assessment, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain said none of the three contenders was in a position to address Nigeria’s challenges. He said, “Look, from my own personal opinion, in my view, voting should depend on who is the person with the right kind of quality and calibre to be able to address the same problem. Peter Obi, Tinubu, Atiku — none of them is there for Nigeria.” The former Jigawa governor also declared his support for the PDP’s presidential candidate, Professor Sandy Onor, insisting that he remained committed to the opposition party and would not vote for Tinubu in 2027. Asked whether he had endorsed Tinubu for a second term, Lamido said he remained a PDP member and would vote for his party’s candidate. He said, “I am PDP through and through. I am voting for my candidate, Professor Sandy Onor; that is my candidate. What I’m saying is that we have somebody called Professor Onor on that ballot. I’m voting him.” Lamido’s remarks come amid controversy over claims that he had endorsed Tinubu’s re-election bid after Vice-President Kashim Shettima reportedly listed him among former Jigawa governors backing the President ahead of 2027. However, the Jigawa State chapter of the PDP had earlier dismissed the claim, insisting that Lamido had neither endorsed Tinubu nor defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. top.title: 3 reasons why Alabama will defeat Vanderbilt in Week 11, 1 why not
top.description: Alabama will be making their first trip to Nashville since their stunning 2024 loss to Vanderbilt this Saturday in Week 11. Alabama (7-2 overall, 5-2 SEC) is on the verge of locking up a spot in the College Football Playoff (CFP), while Vanderbilt (4-5, 1-5) is fighting for bowl eligibility. Last week, Vanderbilt picked up their first win since September with a two-point victory over Mississippi State. That same day, Alabama picked up a big win in a ranked matchup with LSU. What could lead to Alabama improving to 8-2, and what could lead to them potentially suffering a crucial upset loss? Here are three reasons why Alabama will win this week, and one reason they might not. Why: Ryan Coleman-Williams has big day Vanderbilt is one of the teams that Ryan Coleman-Williams has had some of the most success against throughout his career. In the upset loss in 2024, Coleman-Williams had three catches for 82 yards and two touchdowns, one receiving and one two-yard rushing score. Then, last season in Tuscaloosa, he went for six catches for 98 yards and a touchdown. Now that he has worked his way back from injury, this is a chance for Coleman-Williams to fully show that he is back. Why: Alabama forces Vanderbilt to throw the ball A matchup where one of Alabama's strengths matches up with a question mark for Vanderbilt is with Vandy's run game. Vanderbilt has the second-worst rushing attack in the SEC averaging just 112.1 rushing yards per game, while Alabama has a strong run defense, allowing just 104.6 rushing yards per game, fifth-best in the SEC. Those Vanderbilt rushing numbers are even lower just in SEC play. In conference play, Vandy is averaging just 98.5 rushing yards per game. Plus, if Alabama can jump out ahead, Vanderbilt will have to become even more one-dimensional. Why: Alabama forces turnovers One area where being forced into being one-dimensional would hurt Vanderbilt is that, for as much potential as five-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis has, one area that he has struggled is putting the ball in harm's way. So far this season, he has thrown eight interceptions on 224 passing attempts. That is the worst ratio of any SEC quarterback with at least 150 passing attempts this season. Pair that with Alabama's defense being tied for fourth nationally, and leading the SEC, with 13 interceptions as a defensive unit, that bodes well for the Tide. Why not: Letdown spot With Alabama coming off an emotional win on the road in Baton Rouge where they pulled away in the fourth quarter to beat LSU, 31-13, this could be a letdown spot similar to when they lost to Vanderbilt two years ago, which happened the week following their dramatic win over Georgia. With all the talk about Alabama's place in the CFP, if Vanderbilt can catch Alabama sleeping, especially with it being an early start time, then they could make things interesting. top.title: Jack Grealish makes Everton apology after recent antics
top.description: Jack Grealish makes Everton apology after recent antics Jack Grealish Apology Puts Everton Future and Brentford Return in Focus Jack Grealish is back in the frame at Everton after four matches out for what the club described as a breach of discipline. There is no point dressing it up. He let himself down, he let the club down and, by his own admission, he left the team without a player who was supposed to matter. The 31-year-old returned in a behind-closed-doors game against Derby County, a 4-1 win that at least gave him minutes and a route back into contention. Whether it becomes anything more meaningful depends on what comes next, because apologies are easy enough, form and reliability are harder. Everton comeback starts with clear apology Grealish chose a direct approach after his return. “Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training,” Grealish wrote. He then added, “I want to apologise to the fans n (sic) everyone at the club for not been (sic) able to help the team the last few weeks. “I love playing for this club n (sic) can’t wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt. See you all soon.” That is the right message. It had to be. David Moyes backed the disciplinary call and Everton moved on without him for the last four fixtures. Now the burden is on Grealish to show this is not a brief reset followed by the same old issues. Photo IMAGO Brentford return offers Jack Grealish chance His first possible competitive return comes on November 23 away to Brentford. Everton need more than a name on the teamsheet. They need production. So far, Grealish has no goals and no assists in six competitive appearances this season. For an attacking player trying to revive his standing, that is a poor return by any standard. There is another layer here. He is in the final year of his Manchester City contract, and if this spell at Everton is going to lead anywhere, his numbers have to improve quickly. Sentiment does not keep players at clubs, output does. Premier League form remains the real issue There is still a case for believing he can recover his level. Andy Townsend put it bluntly: “If you’re not one of those boys that rocks up in the morning, you’re in great nick from the day before, then you’re not going to survive, certainly not in the Premier League.” He added, “So Jack has got to make a decision (on) what he really wants to do, where he really wants to be and I think find something a little bit more in his game. “A few years ago he had that one season in the treble-winning team where he was truly outstanding there. “Give it to Jack and he’ll hang onto it and he’ll make something happen for us. “That’s disappeared lately. I hope he gets it back.” The record says there was once a high-level player here, 29 Premier League goals, 27 assists and 39 England caps. The recent evidence says Everton are still waiting to see him.

top.title: Sporting Jax soccer boss Mark Warburton to resign. What's next for club?
top.description: Sporting Club Jacksonville president of soccer Mark Warburton will step down from his role with the club on Dec. 1, the organization announced Nov. 13, following a last-place debut season for the professional men's soccer team. Meanwhile, the club announced the new involvement of S&G Sports Ecosystems, headed by former Jacksonville Armada general manager and professional goalkeeper Dario Sala, in a sporting strategy role. Warburton, 64, had supervised Sporting Jax's on-field efforts since his arrival in March 2025, following an extensive coaching career in British soccer with clubs including Brentford and Nottingham Forest in England and Glasgow Rangers in Scotland. He had also served as president of soccer since the March 2026 departure of Steve Livingstone. In a statement, Warburton said it was "the right time for me to seek a new challenge." “Mark helped lay the foundation for soccer at Sporting JAX, and we’re grateful for the work he did to build it,” Sporting Jax owner and executive chairman Ricky Caplin said in a statement. “We thank him for his commitment to the club and to Jacksonville, and we wish him and his family the very best.” While the Sporting Jax women's team within months established itself among the contenders in the Gainbridge Super League, the men's team has brought up the rear in the second-level USL Championship. The Sporting Jax men finished 13th in the Eastern Conference, and 25th and last among all league clubs, in their debut season. They finished 3-22-5 (14 points) with the most goals allowed (78) and a tie for the fewest goals scored (32), more than half of those goals coming from Kieran Sadlier (10 goals, tied for third in the East) or Emil Jaaskelainen (seven goals). The league has announced plans to introduce promotion and relegation between the USL Championship and the third-tier USL League One, but since that system does not take effect until 2028, Sporting Jax is scheduled to continue in the USL Championship in 2027. Sporting Jax has also struggled to draw fans, with several games recording crowds of fewer than 1,000 at the University of North Florida's Hodges Stadium. USL listed an attendance of 712 for the men's Oct. 21 season finale. The club said that Sala, the first general manager of the Jacksonville Armada during North American Soccer League days in 2025, will "lead the engagement" between Sporting Jax and S&G Sports Ecosystems, listed in Florida Department of State records as a Jacksonville-based business founded in March. The club listed roster planning, youth academy opportunities and resource allocation across the men's and women's teams as targets of Sala's review. top.description: Tottenham Hotspur Left-Back Is On The Radar Of Juventus: Should De Zerbi Cash In On Him? In a recent report , Tuttomercatoweb revealed that Tottenham Hotspur left-back Destiny Udogie is on the radar of Juventus. It has been mentioned that the Turin club are eyeing a move to sign the Italian talent next year. Udogie’s Lack Of Game Time In North London Udogie has struggled to secure a regular first-team spot at the North London club in this campaign as he has put in a run of decent displays for them on the left flank. The 23-year-old has made seven appearances for Tottenham this season but has failed to score or create a goal for them in multiple competitions. The Italian talent is currently one of the most talented full-backs in the Premier League . However, he has fallen behind Andy Robertson in Roberto De Zerbi’s pecking order. His current contract at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will run out in the summer of 2030. Hence, Spurs are in no immediate need to cash in on him next year. BIRMINGHAM, ENGLAND – MAY 03: Destiny Udogie of Tottenham Hotspur during the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Tottenham Hotspur at Villa Park on May 03, 2026 in Birmingham, England. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Does Tottenham Hotspur Boss Roberto De Zerbi Cash In On Udogie? Udogie is a good tackler of the ball and can sense the danger well to make some crucial interceptions for his team inside his half. He usually clears the danger when needed and is a decent crosser of the ball. The Italian left-back can even make some driving runs with the ball on the left flank. Udogie is primarily a left-back but can also fill in as a left-sided wide player if asked to do so by his manager. He is already quite familiar with the Premier League and could serve as an important member of Tottenham’s squad this season. However, as mentioned earlier, Udogie is not guaranteed a regular first-team spot at the North London club. Therefore, he might benefit from a change of scenery if he wants to get his career back on track. At 23, Udogie has his peak years ahead of him. Still, De Zerbi would be wise to cash in on him this January, but only if he can bring in a suitable replacement. Another option would be to give Udogie a chance to secure a regular starting place at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium this season and make a decision on his future next summer.

nigeria.title: Nasarawa pensioners begin enforcement of ₦4bn court order
nigeria.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia A group of 601 retired civil servants in Nasarawa State has commenced enforcement of a court order directing the recovery of over ₦4 billion in outstanding gratuities and other entitlements owed them by the state government. The pensioners, under the aegis of the Concerned Group of Nasarawa State Pensioners, secured a consent judgment against the state government in 2020 over the alleged non-payment of their retirement benefits. Their spokespersons, Mr Simon Auna and Mallam Usman Adamu, disclosed the development while speaking with journalists in Lafia on Friday. The group said it subsequently obtained an order from the National Industrial Court, Makurdi, awarding 25 per cent post-judgment interest on the judgment sum, bringing the total amount being sought to over ₦4 billion. According to the pensioners, following the alleged failure of the state government to comply with the judgment, their lawyers approached the Senior District Court in Makurdi, presided over by Justice Ada Jack. The court subsequently directed six commercial banks to release funds belonging to the Nasarawa State Government, amounting to over ₦4 billion, for payment to the affected retirees. In a move to enforce the order, the pensioners’ legal team, accompanied by court bailiffs, visited some branches of one of the commercial banks in Makurdi, Benue State, where they removed some movable properties. Speaking on the development, counsel to the pensioners, Mrs Doofan Sefa-Aii, said the legal team would continue to operate within the law to ensure full recovery of the funds owed the retirees. Another counsel, Mr Awo Matthew, appealed to the Nasarawa State Government and the banks involved to allow the legal process to take its course, considering the hardship the pensioners had endured while pursuing payment of their entitlements. However, the Director of Corporate Services and Arbitration at the Nasarawa State Ministry of Justice, Mr Usman Aliyu, said the state government had taken all necessary legal steps, including filing a motion for a stay of execution of the court order. Meanwhile, Adamu, who is the group’s Lafia Local Government Chairman, and Auna, its Legal Adviser, described the court order as a significant breakthrough after years of seeking payment of their entitlements. They said the development had renewed their hope of recovering the outstanding benefits. The pensioners reaffirmed their determination to pursue their entitlements through lawful means until the matter was resolved. nigeria.title: Zulum offers soldiers N50,000 each, logistics for Borno deployment
nigeria.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced a ₦50,000 welfare support for each soldier preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe communities in the state, alongside a pledge to provide operational logistics to strengthen security. Zulum gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area, where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. The governor said the visit was aimed at exploring measures to improve security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, a strategic economic corridor linking several communities in eastern Borno State. He noted that the highway was vital to trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities, stressing that improved security would enable residents to travel safely, move agricultural produce and rebuild their livelihoods. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe, the governor pledged to provide operational logistics and sustained welfare support. He also announced a payment of ₦50,000 to each soldier preparing for the deployment to the two communities. Koshebe has previously suffered deadly attacks by suspected Boko Haram insurgents. On November 28, 2020, insurgents attacked rice farmers working in fields around the community, killing more than 100 people, many of whom were seasonal farm labourers from Sokoto State. Similarly, in November 2023, suspected insurgents attacked farmers harvesting rice in the Karkut and Koshebe areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 people, while others were reported missing. Zulum’s administration has continued to provide logistics and welfare assistance to security agencies as part of efforts to support military operations, improve security and facilitate the return of displaced residents to their communities. The governor was accompanied on the visit by the member representing Monguno/Nganzai/Marte Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Engr. Bukar Talba; member representing Dikwa Constituency in the Borno State House of Assembly, Mohammed Zakariya; Commissioner for Information and Internal Security, Professor Usman Tar; Commissioner for Local Government and Emirate Affairs, Sugun Mai Mele; and other senior government officials. nigeria.title: COVID-19 loans must be repaid, NIRSAL MFB insists
nigeria.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief NIRSAL Microfinance Bank (NMFB) has clarified that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility (TCF) was an intervention loan, not a grant, stressing that beneficiaries are obligated to repay the funds. The bank said deductions from the accounts of beneficiaries who accessed the facility would continue until their outstanding loans were fully liquidated, in line with the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism. In a statement issued in Abuja at the weekend, the bank explained that the GSI framework allows financial institutions to recover outstanding loan obligations from eligible accounts linked to borrowers’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs), subject to applicable regulatory guidelines. The bank said the clarification became necessary to address concerns surrounding loan recoveries and reassure customers and members of the public of its commitment to transparency, accountability and responsible banking practices. It explained that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility was introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to support households and businesses affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the bank, all beneficiaries were required to accept electronic offer letters before disbursement, with the documents clearly outlining the terms and conditions of the facility, including repayment obligations and recovery mechanisms in cases of default. “Regarding the recovery process, the Bank operates within the applicable regulatory framework, including the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism approved by the Central Bank of Nigeria,” it stated. NIRSAL MFB, however, acknowledged concerns raised by some beneficiaries over the timing and amounts of deductions, outstanding loan balances and access to repayment information. The bank said it took the complaints seriously, noting that customers must have access to accurate information about their loan accounts. It stressed that the deductions were intended to settle outstanding contractual obligations, adding that beneficiaries who disputed deductions or identified discrepancies in their repayment records should contact the bank for individual account reconciliation. “Where any beneficiary has concerns about deductions made, discrepancies in repayment records or the status of an outstanding balance, such cases should be brought to the bank’s attention for individual account reconciliation and appropriate resolution,” it said. The bank assured that legitimate complaints would be investigated and that any discrepancies established during the reconciliation process would receive the necessary attention. It urged beneficiaries seeking clarification on their loan status, repayment history or outstanding obligations to contact the bank through its officially designated customer service channels. nigeria.title: Customs intercepts live sea turtle at Nigeria-Benin border
nigeria.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Seme Area Command, has intercepted a live endangered sea turtle allegedly being smuggled through a footpath linking Nigeria and the Republic of Benin. The Olive Ridley Sea Turtle, scientifically known as Lepidochelys olivacea, was intercepted during a routine patrol by Customs officers at about 10.30pm on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The command said the officers sighted a suspicious individual carrying a sack along the border route, but the suspect abandoned the bag and fled into a nearby bush upon noticing the patrol team. According to a statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Customs, John Tunde Ayagbalo, examination of the abandoned sack revealed the live sea turtle concealed inside. He said the animal was immediately secured and kept in safe custody before being handed over to relevant wildlife authorities for proper care, rehabilitation and eventual release into its natural habitat. The Acting Customs Area Controller, Seme Area Command, Deputy Comptroller Norman Olisah Alumanah, described the interception as a demonstration of the vigilance and professionalism of officers in tackling wildlife trafficking. Alumanah warned smugglers, poachers and their collaborators against using the nation’s borders as corridors for illegal wildlife trade, adding that the command had intensified patrols, surveillance and intelligence gathering across its area of responsibility. He also called on residents of border communities to provide credible intelligence to support the fight against wildlife trafficking. The Customs boss said the command would complement enforcement operations with stakeholder education and sensitisation on endangered species, their ecological importance and the legal implications of their unauthorised trade. Wildlife trafficking remains a major environmental crime, threatening biodiversity and the survival of endangered species through illegal exploitation for meat, eggs, shells, traditional medicine and the exotic pet trade. Nigeria is a signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which regulates international trade in endangered wildlife and plant species. The convention is domesticated in Nigeria through the Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act, Cap E9, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. nigeria.title: Ebola: All 62 contacts test negative after monitoring – NCDC
nigeria.description: By Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has completed the 21-day monitoring of all 62 contacts linked to the imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease (BVD), a form of Ebola disease, confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026, with no secondary infections recorded. The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Friday during a media briefing in Abuja, saying the last contact had been discharged from monitoring after testing negative for the virus. Idris said 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period, but laboratory tests confirmed that none had contracted the disease. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case. “A total of 62 contacts were identified, placed in quarantine and followed up by our public health teams. During the monitoring period, 13 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease, and all tested negative,” he said. The index case was a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman, who tested positive for the virus in Abuja on October 20. She was subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26. Providing an update on her condition, Idris said the woman had recovered and been discharged from a hospital in Geneva. He also disclosed that seven additional suspected cases were reported and investigated in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the past three weeks. All seven cases tested negative for the virus. However, the NCDC chief cautioned against interpreting the completion of contact monitoring as a formal declaration that the outbreak was over. He explained that such a declaration would depend on established public health criteria and findings from continued surveillance. “It is important to note that the completion of contact monitoring does not, by itself, constitute a formal declaration that an outbreak is over. Such a determination must be based on the applicable public health criteria and the findings of ongoing surveillance. “Nigeria therefore remains vigilant, particularly given the continued occurrence of Ebola virus disease in the DRC,” he said. Idris assured Nigerians that disease surveillance and preparedness activities would continue, stressing that the agency remained committed to protecting residents and visitors. Looking ahead to the December festive season, he warned that increased travel, social interactions and large public gatherings could heighten the risk of disease transmission. nigeria.title: 2027: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi not there for Nigeria — Sule Lamido
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Jigawa State Governor and PDP chieftain, Sule Lamido, has dismissed President Bola Tinubu, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, as unsuitable options for Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general election. Lamido stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, where he was asked which of the three political figures could attract the Northern vote in the forthcoming presidential election. Giving his assessment, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain said none of the three contenders was in a position to address Nigeria’s challenges. He said, “Look, from my own personal opinion, in my view, voting should depend on who is the person with the right kind of quality and calibre to be able to address the same problem. Peter Obi, Tinubu, Atiku — none of them is there for Nigeria.” The former Jigawa governor also declared his support for the PDP’s presidential candidate, Professor Sandy Onor, insisting that he remained committed to the opposition party and would not vote for Tinubu in 2027. Asked whether he had endorsed Tinubu for a second term, Lamido said he remained a PDP member and would vote for his party’s candidate. He said, “I am PDP through and through. I am voting for my candidate, Professor Sandy Onor; that is my candidate. What I’m saying is that we have somebody called Professor Onor on that ballot. I’m voting him.” Lamido’s remarks come amid controversy over claims that he had endorsed Tinubu’s re-election bid after Vice-President Kashim Shettima reportedly listed him among former Jigawa governors backing the President ahead of 2027. nigeria.title: NSCDC disbands anti-vandalism outpost after Gombe incident
nigeria.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Gombe State Command, has ordered the immediate disbandment of its Anti-Vandalism Outpost following an incident involving its personnel and a truck driver in the state. The incident, which occurred on Thursday, November 12, 2026, reportedly followed a misunderstanding between personnel of the unit and a truck driver, resulting in the discharge of a firearm. The State Commandant, Commandant Muhammed Inuwa Usman, mni, also summoned all Officers-in-Charge (OCs) of the various formations and outposts to an emergency meeting on Friday to address the incident and reinforce professional standards among personnel. In a statement issued on Friday, the Command’s Public Relations Officer, Chief Superintendent of Corps Buhari Sa’ad, said the meeting was convened to address the incident and strengthen discipline and accountability within the command. During the meeting, Usman cautioned the officers against unprofessional conduct, indiscipline and actions capable of undermining the image of the Corps. He emphasised the need for personnel to remain professional, disciplined and civil, while respecting the fundamental human rights of members of the public in the discharge of their statutory responsibilities. The commandant also stressed that the use of firearms must strictly comply with established rules, operational procedures and applicable regulations, warning officers against taking the law into their own hands. As part of the disciplinary and administrative measures, he ordered the immediate disbandment of the Anti-Vandalism Outpost and directed all personnel attached to the unit to report to the State Command Headquarters without delay. Usman reiterated that the Corps would not condone indiscipline, abuse of authority or violations of citizens’ rights. He urged outpost commanders to strengthen supervision of their personnel and ensure strict adherence to the highest standards of professionalism and accountability. The commandant assured residents that the NSCDC remained committed to protecting lives and property, respecting human rights and maintaining peace and order in Gombe State. nigeria.title: England boss Tuchel eager to end Spain’s unbeaten run
nigeria.description: Thomas Tuchel believes England are ready to end Spain’s unbeaten record when they face the world and European champions in Madrid on Sunday. While victory offers not much more than the prospect of a more favourable Nations League quarter-final in March, it would be a landmark moment for England if they could end Spain’s run of 43 matches without defeat. “It (Spain) is a team that has forgotten how to lose, so of course it requires a top performance first of all, and if we can deliver this performance, it will give us a big boost,” said England manager Tuchel, whose side beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley on Thursday. “I think we’re there, and I think we’re ready to win on Sunday,” the German added. “I know what it takes, and no one can ever guarantee it, but I think it’s the moment to check how far we are and to push our limit and proof of concept.” England lost the reverse fixture 3-2 at Wembley in September, but it might have been a different story had Harry Kane scored a penalty to put Tuchel’s team 3-1 up. “It’s important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home, and attack them and try to make it a physical game, and try to impose our strength.” England players have previously faced racist abuse in Spain, with Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips targeted during a friendly in Madrid in 2004. Spain, meanwhile, must play their next home friendly with a reduced capacity as a punishment for supporters singing a discriminatory chant about Muslims during a fixture against Egypt in March. “We will never accept racism,” said Tuchel. “We will never be racist towards anyone.” He added: “I expect, of course, full support from the Spanish crowd for the Spanish team. But we will not expect anything. And I think the referee and the officials know about that… There is a protocol in place and it’s important that the players know about the protocol. “We will give our answers if stuff like this happens. nigeria.title: Nigeria, EU seal €20m defence support deal
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — Nigeria and the European Union have concluded arrangements for a €20 million defence support package aimed at strengthening the operational capabilities of the Armed Forces, particularly in counterterrorism operations in the Lake Chad Basin. The agreement, the EU’s first bilateral defence support package to Nigeria, is being provided under the European Peace Facility (EPF). The Minister of Defence, Gen. Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.), disclosed this during a meeting with a delegation from the European External Action Service (EEAS), led by the Head of the European Peace Facility, Claire Gaudin, at the Ministry of Defence Headquarters, Ship House, Abuja. According to a statement issued by the Special Assistant (Media) to the minister, Leah Katung-Babatunde, the meeting focused on finalising arrangements for the delivery of the support package, which was sealed in October 2026. Speaking during the meeting, Musa reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to developing indigenous defence capabilities and achieving self-sufficiency in military equipment and technology. He welcomed the EU assistance, describing it as a boost to the operational effectiveness of Nigerian troops engaged in security operations. The minister urged the EU to build on the momentum generated by the recently concluded Africa Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX) by supporting the establishment of local defence production lines in Nigeria. He also reiterated Nigeria’s determination to track and dismantle terrorist financing networks across the world, irrespective of where they operate. Musa explained that the current phase of the EU support would focus on non-lethal military supplies, including equipment, technical training and maintenance. He expressed optimism that subsequent phases would cover other critical areas, particularly military medical support and advanced surveillance capabilities. Earlier, Gaudin said the €20 million package would provide counter-improvised explosive device (C-IED) equipment, counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS), night-vision capabilities and personal protective equipment for troops deployed in operational theatres. She said the priority areas were jointly identified and agreed upon with the leadership of the Armed Forces of Nigeria following extensive bilateral consultations. Gaudin added that Nigeria was among more than 20 African countries and 30 beneficiaries globally receiving assistance under the European Peace Facility. She said the package would complement wider regional stabilisation efforts, particularly operations under the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF). The Nigerian and EU delegations also explored opportunities to deepen security cooperation in maritime operations, with particular attention to strengthening security across the Gulf of Guinea. nigeria.title: Pochettino sheds tears, explains why he left USA for Man Utd
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Mauricio Pochettino broke down in tears as he explained his decision to accept Manchester United’s offer after only recently signing a new contract with the United States national team. The Argentine described leaving the USA job as “one of the most difficult” decisions of his career. According to BBC Sport, Pochettino was announced as Michael Carrick’s successor on Friday and has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford. United triggered a release clause of about £7.4 million, with a further payment for his backroom staff. “It’s difficult to talk now,” Pochettino said at his first news conference after the move was confirmed. “I’m a very emotional guy. nigeria.title: 2027: APC benefits from Atiku, Obi presidential ambitions – Keyamo
nigeria.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has disclosed that the All Progressives Congress (APC) would prefer former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, to participate in the 2027 presidential election to prevent opposition parties from uniting under a single political platform. Keyamo said having both opposition figures on the ballot would serve the ruling party’s political interest by preventing opposition supporters from consolidating their strength behind one candidate. Speaking on Friday during an interview on Frontline, a current affairs programme on Eagle 102.5 FM, Ilese-Ijebu, the minister made the clarification while responding to questions about his earlier comment that heaven would not fall if Atiku Abubakar was absent from the 2027 presidential ballot following the leadership crisis in the African Democratic Congress (ADC). He said, “It is in our interest that Atiku Abubakar and Obi run so that all opposition will not gather under one umbrella.” Keyamo, however, dismissed allegations that the Federal Government or the APC was using state institutions to frustrate opposition parties, insisting that the judiciary was responding to complaints by members of the ADC who felt deprived of their rights during the party’s leadership crisis. He argued that the controversy was being presented as an attempt to prevent a major opposition figure from contesting, while the grievances of other party members who claimed to have been displaced were being overlooked. The minister said, “The judiciary is acting on genuine complaints of Nigerians who are pained. Nigerians who are deprived of their rights in ADC. nigeria.title: Ogun: INEC silent as court orders it to restore Adebutu’s name within 24hrs
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has yet to react officially to a Federal High Court judgment directing it to publish Oladipupo Adebutu’s name as the Peoples Democratic Party PDP candidate for the 2027 Ogun governorship election, saying it only read about the ruling on social media. The Director of Voter Education and Publicity at INEC, Mrs Victoria Messi-Eta, said she read about the judgment in the media and would get a response from the commission’s legal department. As of the time of filing this report, she had yet to revert. The National Commissioner in charge of Voter Education and Publicity, Malam Mohammed Haruna, neither returned calls nor responded to messages sent to him on the matter. The commission’s silence came after Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja ordered INEC on Friday to publish Adebutu’s name within 24 hours. Delivering judgment, Justice Lifu held that INEC had no powers to unilaterally remove the name of a validly nominated candidate by a political party. He held that the commission’s action was unconstitutional, unlawful and of no effect. The judge said only the Federal High Court or the state high court had the power to declare a candidate invalid, not the commission. He also held that INEC breached Adebutu’s right to fair hearing, and dismissed the commission’s preliminary objection, declaring the suit competent. The PDP and Adebutu filed the suit on Oct. 22 after his name was removed from the list of contestants for the Ogun governorship seat. INEC was the sole defendant. Their lawyer, Ahmed Raji, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), sought 11 reliefs, including an order setting aside the commission’s decision to omit, remove or refuse to publish Adebutu’s name in the final list of candidates published on Oct. 10, for denial of fair hearing and violation of Sections 29 and 32 of the Electoral Act, 2026. They also asked the court to compel “the defendant to, within twenty-four (24) hours of the order/orders of this honourable court, include and/or publish the name of the 2nd plaintiff as the 1st plaintiff’s governorship candidate for Ogun State in the forthcoming 2027 General Election.” The post Ogun: INEC silent as court orders it to restore Adebutu’s name within 24hrs appeared first on Vanguard News .

Ouagadougou Court of Appeal attorney general Desire Sawadogo said 14 arrest warrants with extradition requests had been issued, alongside seven further standard warrants. Burkina Faso, mired in jihadist violence for a decade, is governed by a junta that seized power in September 2022. It has cracked down hard on any criticism. Those targeted include Newton Ahmed Barry, a journalist for Radio France Internationale as well as former foreign minister Djibril Bassole, several officers and cyberactivists. They are accused of “complicity in forming a terrorist criminal organisation and complicity in the financing of terrorism”, as well as “forming a terrorist criminal organisation”, “glorifying terrorism” and “incitement to rebellion”. Also among those targeted, albeit not by a warrant, is the Ivorian influencer Camille Makosso, known for diatribes against Sahel region juntas and who has some four million social media followers. The justice ministry said Friday evening it was calling for legal proceedings in his country of residence” and hoped Ivory Coast would heed the request “in the name of international judicial cooperation.” Sawadogo said “media such as France 24” were also in the authorities’ sights. According to the prosecutor, more than six cases involving over 45 individuals and legal entities are currently under investigation by Burkina Faso’s specialised anti-terror judicial unit. The compact home miner, which also runs a full bitcoin node, will be sold in Brooklyn, Miami, Tustin, California, and Austin, Texas, as those stores open Friday, FutureBit said in a release. The four-store launch coincides with the grand opening of Micro Center’s new Austin store, the chain’s 31st U.S. location and its third in Texas. Customers will also be able to reserve a unit online for in-store pickup, the company said. It did not say how many units each store has in stock, or what Micro Center is charging for them. Until now, buyers in North America had to order the machine from FutureBit’s website, where the company says units are in stock and ship in two to three days. Putting it on a computer-store shelf lets a customer look at the hardware, ask how it works and carry it out the same day. “When we started FutureBit, we made weekly trips to the DIY electronics section at the Brooklyn Micro Center to buy parts,” said John Stefanopoulos, founder of FutureBit. “On Friday, someone can walk into that same store, ask how Bitcoin mining works and take home a miner we designed just down the street. We couldn’t be more excited to work with Micro Center on our first physical store launch.” A 6-inch miner that also runs a full node FutureBit’s own shop lists the Apollo III Full Node at $1,099.99 without a storage drive, $1,299.99 with 1 terabyte of SSD storage and $1,399.99 with 2 terabytes. A cheaper, miner-only “Standard” model starts at $899.99 but does not include the full node. The Full Node is rated at up to 18 terahashes per second in Turbo mode, at about 325 watts. In Eco mode, it is listed at about 12 TH/s and 150 watts, with noise under 35 decibels. A Super Eco mode is listed at about 8 TH/s and 80 watts. Power can be adjusted from 50 to 400 watts, and Turbo mode is much louder, at about 55 decibels. Those power figures are measured at the board and can vary by 10%, the product page says. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double Crypto trading on Robinhood fell by almost half from a year ago in October, the company said Thursday , as customers traded $17 billion of digital assets while their bets on event contracts more than doubled. The $17 billion figure was down 21% from September and 48% from October 2025, when crypto notional volume reached $32.5 billion. It covers both the flagship Robinhood app and Bitstamp, the crypto exchange the company bought in 2025. Volume in the Robinhood app fell to $6.8 billion, down 24% from September and 51% from a year earlier. Bitstamp handled $10.2 billion, down 18% month over month and 45% year over year. Average daily crypto volume across both platforms came to $548 million, compared with $713 million in September and about $1.05 billion a year ago. Daily average crypto trades slipped to about 700,000 from 900,000 in September and 1.1 million in October 2025. Event contracts take off as crypto cools The contrast with Robinhood’s prediction markets business is stark. Customers traded 5.9 billion event contracts in October, up 5% from September and 136% from the 2.5 billion traded a year earlier. Average daily volume reached 190 million contracts. Robinhood counts crypto and prediction markets on the same 31-day calendar, since both trade every day, so the comparison is apples to apples. Event contracts let users bet on outcomes such as elections, sports and economic data, and October’s tally covered the final weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections. That growth has drawn scrutiny in Washington. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, who is set to chair the Senate Banking Committee in January, plans to crack down on prediction markets and election betting platforms. The rest of Robinhood’s brokerage held up better than crypto. Equity notional volume rose 2% from a year earlier to $325 billion, and options contracts traded climbed 8% to 289 million. Margin balances reached $22.9 billion, up 39% year over year. Funded customers rose by about 130,000 in the month to 28.9 million, and net deposits came to $15.1 billion. Total platform assets slipped 3% from September to $383 billion but were up 12% from a year earlier. Robinhood did not say why crypto activity fell. business.title: President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed President Donald Trump sent the Senate four nominees for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Thursday, his first picks for either agency in about a year and the first Democrats he has put forward for them. Former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson, a Democrat, and Republican Steven Levine were nominated to the SEC. Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland were nominated to the CFTC, Bloomberg Law reported. Each nominee needs Senate confirmation. The Senate Banking Committee will handle the SEC picks, while the Senate Agriculture Committee will take up the CFTC pair before any vote by the full chamber. Who the nominees are Levine was tapped for the SEC seat left by Hester Peirce, whose term expired, for a term running through June 5, 2030. He most recently served as general counsel and a senior adviser at the White House Council of Economic Advisers and previously worked at the SEC as counsel and deputy chief of staff to Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Peirce led the SEC’s Crypto Task Force and was one of the agency’s most vocal supporters of clearer crypto rules. Johnson would take the seat formerly held by Democrat Caroline Crenshaw, for a term ending June 5, 2029. She served as a CFTC commissioner until 2025 and is a former law school professor. During her time at the CFTC, she spoke often about digital assets, including custody and decentralized finance. Both CFTC nominees come from the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the derivatives regulator. Anonick is legislative counsel to Chairman John Boozman and was a lead negotiator on the committee’s portion of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031. Rowland is a CFTC attorney detailed to the committee who also worked on the Clarity Act and the committee’s 2024 crypto bill. He previously served on Johnson’s staff at the CFTC, according to his LinkedIn profile. He would fill the remainder of former Commissioner Summer Mersinger’s term, which expires April 13, 2028. Both agencies can seat up to five commissioners, with no more than three from one party. The SEC currently has two, Chairman Paul Atkins and Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Chairman Mike Selig is the CFTC’s only sitting commissioner. Lame-duck timing and a Democratic Senate The timing puts the nominees in front of a Senate in its lame-duck session, weeks after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, one of crypto’s sharpest critics, is expected to chair the Banking Committee when the new Congress is seated in January. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. sports.title: 3 reasons why Alabama will defeat Vanderbilt in Week 11, 1 why not
sports.description: Alabama will be making their first trip to Nashville since their stunning 2024 loss to Vanderbilt this Saturday in Week 11. Alabama (7-2 overall, 5-2 SEC) is on the verge of locking up a spot in the College Football Playoff (CFP), while Vanderbilt (4-5, 1-5) is fighting for bowl eligibility. Last week, Vanderbilt picked up their first win since September with a two-point victory over Mississippi State. That same day, Alabama picked up a big win in a ranked matchup with LSU. What could lead to Alabama improving to 8-2, and what could lead to them potentially suffering a crucial upset loss? Here are three reasons why Alabama will win this week, and one reason they might not. Why: Ryan Coleman-Williams has big day Vanderbilt is one of the teams that Ryan Coleman-Williams has had some of the most success against throughout his career. In the upset loss in 2024, Coleman-Williams had three catches for 82 yards and two touchdowns, one receiving and one two-yard rushing score. Then, last season in Tuscaloosa, he went for six catches for 98 yards and a touchdown. Now that he has worked his way back from injury, this is a chance for Coleman-Williams to fully show that he is back. Why: Alabama forces Vanderbilt to throw the ball A matchup where one of Alabama's strengths matches up with a question mark for Vanderbilt is with Vandy's run game. Vanderbilt has the second-worst rushing attack in the SEC averaging just 112.1 rushing yards per game, while Alabama has a strong run defense, allowing just 104.6 rushing yards per game, fifth-best in the SEC. Those Vanderbilt rushing numbers are even lower just in SEC play. In conference play, Vandy is averaging just 98.5 rushing yards per game. Plus, if Alabama can jump out ahead, Vanderbilt will have to become even more one-dimensional. Why: Alabama forces turnovers One area where being forced into being one-dimensional would hurt Vanderbilt is that, for as much potential as five-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis has, one area that he has struggled is putting the ball in harm's way. So far this season, he has thrown eight interceptions on 224 passing attempts. That is the worst ratio of any SEC quarterback with at least 150 passing attempts this season. Pair that with Alabama's defense being tied for fourth nationally, and leading the SEC, with 13 interceptions as a defensive unit, that bodes well for the Tide. Why not: Letdown spot With Alabama coming off an emotional win on the road in Baton Rouge where they pulled away in the fourth quarter to beat LSU, 31-13, this could be a letdown spot similar to when they lost to Vanderbilt two years ago, which happened the week following their dramatic win over Georgia. With all the talk about Alabama's place in the CFP, if Vanderbilt can catch Alabama sleeping, especially with it being an early start time, then they could make things interesting. sports.title: Jack Grealish makes Everton apology after recent antics
sports.description: Jack Grealish makes Everton apology after recent antics Jack Grealish Apology Puts Everton Future and Brentford Return in Focus Jack Grealish is back in the frame at Everton after four matches out for what the club described as a breach of discipline. There is no point dressing it up. He let himself down, he let the club down and, by his own admission, he left the team without a player who was supposed to matter. The 31-year-old returned in a behind-closed-doors game against Derby County, a 4-1 win that at least gave him minutes and a route back into contention. Whether it becomes anything more meaningful depends on what comes next, because apologies are easy enough, form and reliability are harder. Everton comeback starts with clear apology Grealish chose a direct approach after his return. “Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training,” Grealish wrote. He then added, “I want to apologise to the fans n (sic) everyone at the club for not been (sic) able to help the team the last few weeks. “I love playing for this club n (sic) can’t wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt. See you all soon.” That is the right message. It had to be. David Moyes backed the disciplinary call and Everton moved on without him for the last four fixtures. Now the burden is on Grealish to show this is not a brief reset followed by the same old issues. Photo IMAGO Brentford return offers Jack Grealish chance His first possible competitive return comes on November 23 away to Brentford. Everton need more than a name on the teamsheet. They need production. So far, Grealish has no goals and no assists in six competitive appearances this season. For an attacking player trying to revive his standing, that is a poor return by any standard. There is another layer here. He is in the final year of his Manchester City contract, and if this spell at Everton is going to lead anywhere, his numbers have to improve quickly. Sentiment does not keep players at clubs, output does. Premier League form remains the real issue There is still a case for believing he can recover his level. Andy Townsend put it bluntly: “If you’re not one of those boys that rocks up in the morning, you’re in great nick from the day before, then you’re not going to survive, certainly not in the Premier League.” He added, “So Jack has got to make a decision (on) what he really wants to do, where he really wants to be and I think find something a little bit more in his game. “A few years ago he had that one season in the treble-winning team where he was truly outstanding there. “Give it to Jack and he’ll hang onto it and he’ll make something happen for us. “That’s disappeared lately. I hope he gets it back.” The record says there was once a high-level player here, 29 Premier League goals, 27 assists and 39 England caps. The recent evidence says Everton are still waiting to see him.

sports.title: Sporting Jax soccer boss Mark Warburton to resign. What's next for club?
sports.description: Sporting Club Jacksonville president of soccer Mark Warburton will step down from his role with the club on Dec. 1, the organization announced Nov. 13, following a last-place debut season for the professional men's soccer team. Meanwhile, the club announced the new involvement of S&G Sports Ecosystems, headed by former Jacksonville Armada general manager and professional goalkeeper Dario Sala, in a sporting strategy role. Warburton, 64, had supervised Sporting Jax's on-field efforts since his arrival in March 2025, following an extensive coaching career in British soccer with clubs including Brentford and Nottingham Forest in England and Glasgow Rangers in Scotland. He had also served as president of soccer since the March 2026 departure of Steve Livingstone. In a statement, Warburton said it was "the right time for me to seek a new challenge." “Mark helped lay the foundation for soccer at Sporting JAX, and we’re grateful for the work he did to build it,” Sporting Jax owner and executive chairman Ricky Caplin said in a statement. “We thank him for his commitment to the club and to Jacksonville, and we wish him and his family the very best.” While the Sporting Jax women's team within months established itself among the contenders in the Gainbridge Super League, the men's team has brought up the rear in the second-level USL Championship. The Sporting Jax men finished 13th in the Eastern Conference, and 25th and last among all league clubs, in their debut season. They finished 3-22-5 (14 points) with the most goals allowed (78) and a tie for the fewest goals scored (32), more than half of those goals coming from Kieran Sadlier (10 goals, tied for third in the East) or Emil Jaaskelainen (seven goals). The league has announced plans to introduce promotion and relegation between the USL Championship and the third-tier USL League One, but since that system does not take effect until 2028, Sporting Jax is scheduled to continue in the USL Championship in 2027. Sporting Jax has also struggled to draw fans, with several games recording crowds of fewer than 1,000 at the University of North Florida's Hodges Stadium. sports.title: MLB lockout watch: Will free agency and trades speed up before Dec. 1?
sports.description: As the expiration of MLB's current collective bargaining agreement approaches , it's worth taking a look back at what unfolded five years ago as potentially instructive for what to expect leading up to a lockout instituted by MLB's team owners that would freeze all major-league transactions leaguewide. One clear trend in 2021 was an uncommon rush of activity in free agency in the handful of days leading up to the lockout, with a bevy of big names signing massive contracts before moves ceased for months until a new CBA was eventually agreed upon on March 10. But inspect the transaction logs from that November five years ago, and another pattern emerges. "If you just look back, there weren't a large number of trades," Toronto Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins said at the GM Meetings in Las Vegas earlier this week. "There were signings — there was a lot of money spent early — but not a lot of trades." Indeed, there was a distinct lack of trade activity mirroring the frenzy of free-agent deals that dramatically altered rosters across the league before the lockout went into effect in 2021. The biggest blockbuster trades of that offseason were not executed until the lockout was lifted in March. Atkins and the Blue Jays embodied this dynamic. Toronto was responsible for one of the largest free-agent contracts given out during the mad dash before the CBA expired, landing right-hander Kevin Gausman with a five-year, $110 million deal. And Gausman's wasn't even among the top five most lucrative deals agreed to leading up to the lockout. There were Corey Seager (10 years, $325 million) and Marcus Semien (seven years, $175 million) with the Texas Rangers, Javier Báez (six years, $140 million) with the Detroit Tigers, Max Scherzer (three years, $130 million) with the New York Mets and Robbie Ray (five years, $115 million) with the Seattle Mariners. Jake Bauers was the biggest name to move in the free-agent market this month. AP Photo/Gregory Bull Gausman represented a bold first strike for the Blue Jays. But their next biggest move that offseason didn't happen until March: The acquisition of Gold Glove third baseman Matt Chapman from the Athletics in exchange for four prospects. This was the finale of a trio of significant trades executed by the A’s in the week after the lockout ended, following deals that sent right-hander Chris Bassitt to the Mets and first baseman Matt Olson to the Braves. Cincinnati was busy in similar fashion once the moves resumed in March, trading veteran starter Sonny Gray to the Minnesota Twins and sluggers Jesse Winker and Eugenio Suárez to the Mariners. The Reds and Athletics' selloff swaps headlined a series of trades leading up to the delayed Opening Day in 2022 that also featured the Twins sending Mitch Garver to the Rangers and Josh Donaldson to the New York Yankees. sports.description: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Wild (14-3-4) haven’t lost in regulation in 10 games , going 8-0-2 in that stretch. Thursday’s 5-2 win in Toronto also brought their road winning streak to seven games, tied for the second-longest in franchise history. The victory also brought the Wild’s point total to 32, which is only one more point than the Edmonton Oilers. However, they now sit seven points ahead of Central Division rivals Nashville and Colorado (25 points). Only the Carolina Hurricanes, out in the Eastern Conference, has as many points as the Wild. It’s still only mid-November, and Minnesota still has 63 games left on their new 84-game schedule. But the hot start has been so good that we can at least lock one thing in for this spring… or so the models say. Minnesota Wild playoff odds hit 98% in The Athletic’s model According to Dom Luszczyszyn who ran the numbers past The Athletic’s postseason projection model Friday morning on the Wild’s live blog . Do you believe in robots? If so, then you can sleep soundly at night knowing the MN Wild are pretty much a lock (98%) to make the playoffs in 2026-27. It’s the highest playoff odds and projected point total of any team in the Central. Beyond the 98% playoff chance, the model gives the Wild a 48% chance to win the Central, a 14% chance at the Presidents’ Trophy and a 9% chance to win the Stanley Cup.
